isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

+publication remain TP1. See the [mechanics recipe](core.md#checkpoints-and-publication)

"""Keep the end of a training process bounded.

Closing tracking runs in a daemon thread with a deadline, so a stuck flush cannot
hold the driver. When it finishes, the CLI exits through normal interpreter
shutdown (atexit handlers, Ray's own shutdown), with a watchdog that forces the
exit if that shutdown itself hangs. When a bounded operation was abandoned, its
thread may still hold the process, so the CLI shuts down driver-owned Ray and
then ends the process with os._exit, keeping the success or failure exit code.
"""

import contextlib
import faulthandler
import logging
import os
import sys
import threading
import traceback

from open_instruct import logger_utils

logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)

TRACKING_CLOSE_TIMEOUT = 120
RAY_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 60
# Upper bound on normal interpreter shutdown after the result is recorded.
EXIT_WATCHDOG_SECONDS = 300
# Logging, flushing and stderr writes can block on locks an abandoned or stuck
# thread holds, or on a full output pipe, so on the forced-exit paths they run in a
# daemon thread for at most this long.
LOCKED_IO_TIMEOUT = 5

# Names of bounded operations whose threads were abandoned in this process.
_abandoned = []
# Set by the CLI entry point only, so importing callers (and tests) never get a timer
# that ends their process.
_exit_watchdog_enabled = False


def run_bounded(operation, name, timeout=TRACKING_CLOSE_TIMEOUT):
    """Run ``operation`` in a daemon thread for at most ``timeout`` seconds.

    Returns True when it returned or raised, False on timeout. Its exceptions are
    logged, not raised: a tracking backend that fails to close must not turn a
    training run whose result is recorded into a failure. On timeout the thread is
    abandoned with a warning and a stack dump of every thread, and ``abandoned()``
    reports it so the CLI can force the process exit.
    """

    def target():
        try:
            operation()
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("%s failed", name)

    thread = threading.Thread(target=target, name=f"bounded-{name}", daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    thread.join(timeout)
    if thread.is_alive():
        _abandoned.append(name)

        def report():
            logger.warning("%s did not finish within %ss; continuing shutdown without it", name, timeout)
            faulthandler.dump_traceback(all_threads=True)

        _bounded(report)
        return False
    return True


def _bounded(call, timeout=None):
    """Run ``call`` in a daemon thread and wait at most ``timeout`` seconds for it."""
    thread = threading.Thread(target=call, name="bounded-io", daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    thread.join(LOCKED_IO_TIMEOUT if timeout is None else timeout)


def abandoned():
    return list(_abandoned)


def finish_process(code):
    """End the CLI with ``code`` once the run's result is recorded.

    If a bounded operation was abandoned, shut down driver-owned Ray and exit now:
    the abandoned thread could otherwise keep the process alive. Otherwise return,

diff --git a/docs/miles/operations.md b/docs/miles/operations.md
index de23367cc..731414f0b 100644
--- a/docs/miles/operations.md
+++ b/docs/miles/operations.md
@@ -97,6 +97,21 @@ reward filtering. A short error burst cannot become fatal just because no more
 requests finish. The check runs while waiting for generation or buffer space,
 not only at optimizer boundaries.
 
+A separate limit stops a run when one prompt group keeps failing while other
+generation succeeds: after `core.max_group_retries` isolated retries (default 3),
+the group's next failure is fatal. Failures with no successful generation in
+between are left to the 50% rule. Every group attempt draws the same risk, so
+the chance of hitting the limit grows with run length. On three OLMo 3.5 Small
+runs (November 2026), 205 of 28,053 group attempts failed with router transport
+errors (0.73%). The failures came in bursts across many groups, not repeatedly
+on one prompt: one group failed twice, against about 1.5 expected by chance.
+At that rate, a 660-update run at 2,048 responses per update (roughly 170,000-260,000 group
+attempts) has about a 0.05-0.2% chance of some group reaching a fourth failure
+with the default. The chance is about 3-4% if the failure rate rises to 2%. For
+multi-day runs, set `core.max_group_retries = 5`, which brings the 2% case to
+about 1e-5. It takes effect only with a MILES pin that reads the field
+(allenai/miles-olmo-core#55); older pins keep 3.
+
 Unknown HTTP/server errors, invalid configuration, and invalid sample/policy
 provenance remain fatal. Only typed generation deadlines are recoverable; an
 unrelated timeout is not automatically treated as a serving failure. Server-side
@@ -142,6 +157,29 @@ client window removes this race without the extra connection churn of a shorter
 client expiry. Preserve error reporting and whole-group recovery; do not silently
 retry ambiguous generation requests at the HTTP layer.
 
+### Router TCP_USER_TIMEOUT shim
+
+The pinned Rust sgl-router (0.3.2, reqwest 0.12.28) sets `TCP_USER_TIMEOUT=30s`
+on its upstream engine connections. With TCP keepalive on, one lost keepalive
+probe then resets a healthy in-flight non-streaming `/generate` about 15 seconds
+later; the router returns 500 `call_upstream_request_error` and the whole group

"""Check an HF export's KDA weights against the OLMo-core checkpoint it was converted from, exactly.

Five tensors per KDA layer can be float32 in a training forward: `A_log`, `dt_bias` and the `q/k/v_conv1d` weights.
An export must store the value the forward used (see convert_moe_checkpoint_to_hf.py, `--kda-decay`). This reads
those tensors from the export's safetensors and from the checkpoint and compares every element:

    uv run python scripts/train/debug/check_kda_export.py \
        --checkpoint <ckpt>/step172 --hf-dir <ckpt>/hf_step172 --kda-decay fp32

- `--kda-decay fp32`: all five are float32 in the export and equal the checkpoint's float32 values.
- `--kda-decay bf16-grid`: `A_log` and `dt_bias` are float32, the convolution weights bfloat16, and all five equal
  the checkpoint's values rounded to the bfloat16 grid.

It is a mechanism check: it passes or fails on equality, prints one line per tensor that differs, writes the
result as JSON with `--output`, and exits 1 on any difference. It reads files only. It does not show what a
serving stack holds after loading the export.
"""

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys
import tempfile

import torch
from olmo_core.distributed.checkpoint import get_checkpoint_metadata, load_keys
from safetensors import safe_open

from open_instruct import logger_utils

logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)

DECAY = ("A_log", "dt_bias")
CONVS = ("q_conv1d.weight", "k_conv1d.weight", "v_conv1d.weight")
MODES = ("bf16-grid", "fp32")


def kda_layers(hf_dir: pathlib.Path) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the export's KDA layers, from its config.json."""
    layer_types = json.loads((hf_dir / "config.json").read_text())["layer_types"]
    return [index for index, kind in enumerate(layer_types) if kind == "linear_attention"]


def checkpoint_kda_layers(checkpoint: pathlib.Path) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the checkpoint's KDA layers: the blocks that store an ``attention.A_log``."""
    stored = get_checkpoint_metadata(str(checkpoint / "model_and_optim")).state_dict_metadata
    found = (re.search(r"(?:^|\.)blocks\.(\d+)\.attention\.A_log(?:\.main)?$", key) for key in stored)
    return sorted({int(match[1]) for match in found if match})

# Running SFT on TPU: a known-good starting point

Olmo 3.5 tiny (`olmo35-tiny`, the 4T EMO base, called "small" before 2026-11) on Dolci-Think with H045's recipe, on **one TPU v4 `4x4x8` slice (128 chips)** of
the `gke-tpu-v4` cluster, through MaxText + Tunix.

Measured cost and outcome: 11,768 steps of 16 × 65,536 tokens at a median 3.94 s/step, 13.5 h wall clock from submit
to the last step. The loss matches H045's GPU runs (parity windows in [open-instruct#1933](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/issues/1933)). The GPU recipe takes 5 h 54 m on
2×8 H100, so the TPU path is slower per run. Its advantage is capacity: three of these runs fit at once without
touching Beaker.

The recipe is `scripts/tpu/maxtext/k8s/olmo35-sft-4x4x8/`.
Its `kustomization.yaml` header records why each setting is what it is; read it before editing. Olmo 3 7B has its
own overlay, `k8s/instruct-sft-4x4x8/`; its base `k8s/olmo3-sft/` targets a `2x2x4` slice, which no longer exists. `scripts/tpu/maxtext/README.md` lists the MaxText patches.

## Example runs

| Run | What it is |
|---|---|
| `olmo35-sft-h045-tpu-full-r2` | This recipe, verbatim: the TPU replica of the ledger's H045 anchor (arm `anchor-emo-olmo35-tpu`). 0 restarts, final CE 0.9245. HF export: `/weka/oe-adapt-default/abhishekr/tpu-posttrain/hf/olmo35-sft-h045-tpu-full-r2-step11768`. |
| H067, H072 (olmo-post-training-ledger) | The same recipe with other data: arms, seeds, resumes and their checks are recorded in those hypothesis files and in [open-instruct#1976](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/issues/1976) and [#1977](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/issues/1977). |

"""Check an HF export's KDA weights against the OLMo-core checkpoint it was converted from, exactly.

Five tensors per KDA layer can be float32 in a training forward: `A_log`, `dt_bias` and the `q/k/v_conv1d` weights.
An export must store the value the forward used (see convert_moe_checkpoint_to_hf.py, `--kda-decay`). This reads
those tensors from the export's safetensors and from the checkpoint and compares every element:

    uv run python scripts/train/debug/check_kda_export.py \
        --checkpoint <ckpt>/step172 --hf-dir <ckpt>/hf_step172 --kda-decay fp32

- `--kda-decay fp32`: all five are float32 in the export and equal the checkpoint's float32 values.
- `--kda-decay bf16-grid`: `A_log` and `dt_bias` are float32, the convolution weights bfloat16, and all five equal
  the checkpoint's values rounded to the bfloat16 grid.

It is a mechanism check: it passes or fails on equality, prints one line per tensor that differs, writes the
result as JSON with `--output`, and exits 1 on any difference. It reads files only. It does not show what a
serving stack holds after loading the export.
"""

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys
import tempfile

import torch
from olmo_core.distributed.checkpoint import get_checkpoint_metadata, load_keys
from safetensors import safe_open

from open_instruct import logger_utils

logger = logger_utils.setup_logger(__name__)

DECAY = ("A_log", "dt_bias")
CONVS = ("q_conv1d.weight", "k_conv1d.weight", "v_conv1d.weight")
MODES = ("bf16-grid", "fp32")


def kda_layers(hf_dir: pathlib.Path) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the export's KDA layers, from its config.json."""
    layer_types = json.loads((hf_dir / "config.json").read_text())["layer_types"]
    return [index for index, kind in enumerate(layer_types) if kind == "linear_attention"]


def checkpoint_kda_layers(checkpoint: pathlib.Path) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of the checkpoint's KDA layers: the blocks that store an ``attention.A_log``."""
    stored = get_checkpoint_metadata(str(checkpoint / "model_and_optim")).state_dict_metadata
    found = (re.search(r"(?:^|\.)blocks\.(\d+)\.attention\.A_log(?:\.main)?$", key) for key in stored)
    return sorted({int(match[1]) for match in found if match})

+### Re-rendering prepared prompts for a new start checkpoint
+
+When the start checkpoint changes, its chat template can differ from the one the
+prepared prompts were rendered with, even when the rendered text would not change.
+Data preparation then stops with "Prepared rendering template hash differs from the
+checkpoint chat template; re-render inputs". Re-render the prompts with the new
+checkpoint's tokenizer before launching:
+
+```bash
+python -m scripts.miles.rerender_prompts INPUT.jsonl.gz NEW_CHECKPOINT OUTPUT.jsonl.gz
+```
+
+The tool renders `metadata.messages` with the checkpoint's chat template and
+recomputes the template hash and saved prompt token fields. MILES rebuilds its
+run-specific token cache for the new export. Tool rows also use
+their saved function declarations and must be compatible with the new template's
+tool-call protocol. ToolRL's `think_prefix_in_prompt` is recomputed in the label
+and verifier target. An older structured tool export without saved declarations
+needs to be exported again before it can be re-rendered.
+
+The command writes a new file atomically using a hard link. It stops on an
+unsupported row or if the output or report already exists. The report records
+file hashes, template hashes, and how many prompts changed. Point
+`data.prompt_data` at the output in a new run root. Qualification receipts bound
+to the old file hash do not carry over. For a new Workbench release with
+updated qualification evidence, render and export from the canonical collection.
+
+Prepared files and checkpoints are usually on WEKA, so run the tool as a small CPU
+Beaker job. Use an image built from open-instruct at or after this tool was added
+(the launcher's MILES image works: the repository is at `/opt/core-rl`). Mount every
+bucket the checkpoint's files link into (SFT exports on `olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints`
+can be symlinks into `olmo-3p5-checkpoints`):
+
+```yaml
+version: v2
+budget: ai2/oe-other
+tasks:
+  - name: rerender-prompts
+    image: {beaker: IMMUTABLE_IMAGE_ID}
+    command: [bash, -c]
+    arguments:
+      - >-
+        cd /opt/core-rl && python -m scripts.miles.rerender_prompts
+        /weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/robertb/miles/h196-dolci-control-20261113/inputs/dolci.jsonl.gz
+        /weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/PATH/TO/NEW_CHECKPOINT
+        /weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/YOUR_USERNAME/miles/inputs/dolci-NEW.jsonl.gz
+    datasets:
+      - {mountPath: /weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints, source: {weka: olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints}}
+      - {mountPath: /weka/olmo-3p5-checkpoints, source: {weka: olmo-3p5-checkpoints}}
+    resources: {gpuCount: 0, cpuCount: 8, memory: 64GiB}
+    context: {priority: high, preemptible: true}
+    constraints: {cluster: [ai2/holmes, ai2/jupiter]}
+    timeout: 2h
+    result: {path: /output}
+```
+
+Submit it with `beaker experiment create rerender.yaml --workspace ai2/olmo-instruct`.
+Re-rendering the 84,577 H196 Dolci rows for the H258 SFT export took one such job
+(Beaker 01M7WAR5PQHAE30C4DXWYP10XH, with the prototype of this script): every input was
+byte-identical and only the template hash changed.

# Olmo 3.5 Small (A4B) text SFT on the 3,072-chip v4 8x8x48: the 3K hero recipe of the olmo-post-training-ledger's
# experiments/h269/render.py (H262's causal r1 files, h262-3k/), production settings. 96 x 65,536 tokens a step on
# data24 x FSDP4 x EP32 (olmo35-ep-as-cp, context load balancing off, 4 rows on each of 24 data hosts), LR 1.8e-4 with
# 3% warmup then linear to 0 at LR_SCHEDULE_STEPS, causal EMO, ragged buffer 14 with REQUIRED_RBF and MOE-DROPPED
# logged every step, a save every 500 updates and 30 kept, a 24 h JobSet deadline.
# What differs from that render: MaxText is the fork commit in maxtext_source (abhishekraok/maxtext b4fabf77, branch
# small-sft-3k: upstream d7287433 + the SFT port + the host-side (np) tail mask and log tail + causal EMO, the tree
# render.py's launcher builds with four patches), with no patch step; pos_ce.patch, a logging-only diagnostic for
# preflights, is not on it; and the launcher refuses the CHANGE_ME placeholders below.
# Per run: RUN_NAME, LOAD_PARAMETERS_PATH, TRAIN_FILES, STEPS = LR_SCHEDULE_STEPS (a stream's RECEIPT.json final_update).
# NUM_EPOCH=1 and enable_data_shuffling=false read a stream whose order is materialized in its files.
# EMO off is render.py --emo off: in EXTRA_ARGS, emo_enabled=false moe_topk_pallas=true and drop the other emo_* flags.
#   kubectl kustomize . | less     # check the render
#   kubectl --context gke_ai2-olmo_us-central2-b_gke-tpu-v4 create -k .
# The JobSet is immutable and created suspended (Kueue admits it). To resume or relaunch, delete all three objects first
# (kubectl delete -k .): create does not update an existing ConfigMap, so a JobSet created beside one would read stale
# settings. Not apply -k: re-applying suspend: true to an admitted JobSet could suspend it.
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: olmo

resources:
- jobset.yaml

generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true

configMapGenerator:
- name: olmo35-small-sft-8x8x48-launcher
  files:
  - train_sft_perf.sh
  - perf_wrapper.py # MaxText train_sft plus the env switches its docstring lists (SKIP_FINAL_SAVE, FORCE_NNX_CACHE, ...)
  - maxtext_source # The MaxText fork and commit the launcher runs: the one place to bump.
- name: olmo35-small-sft-8x8x48-env
  literals:
  # Set a unique name before launching; checkpoints go to OUTPUT_DIR/RUN_NAME.
  - RUN_NAME=CHANGE_ME
  - OUTPUT_DIR=gs://ai2-olmo-dev/olmo-3p5-maxtext/sft-runs
  # gs://.../<step>/items of the start (H262's: gs://ai2-olmo-dev/olmo-3p5-maxtext/sft-bases/olmo35-small-14t-decay548k-200b-think-seeded/556000/items).
  - LOAD_PARAMETERS_PATH=CHANGE_ME
  - TOKENIZER_PATH=/mnt/post-training/tokenizers/olmo35-03c29652-c12rf-promoted
  # A stream under gs://ai2-olmo-dev/post-training/data/ (e.g. hero-3k/streams/<stream>/data).
  - TRAIN_FILES=/mnt/post-training/data/CHANGE_ME/*.parquet
  - MODEL_NAME=olmo35-small-e256k8-sh2x
  - MAXTEXT_SFT_LABELS=prefix
  - MAXTEXT_SFT_TAIL_MASK_ONLY=1
  - TOTAL_DEVICES=3072
  - GLOBAL_BATCH=96
  - PER_DEVICE_BATCH=0.03125
  - SEQ_LEN=65536
  - LR=1.8e-4
  # EXTRA_ARGS' wsd_decay_steps_fraction=0.97 overrides the launcher's 1 - WARMUP_FRAC: change the two together.
  - WARMUP_FRAC=0.03
  - LR_SCHEDULE_STEPS=CHANGE_ME
  - STEPS=CHANGE_ME
  - NUM_EPOCH=1
  - DATA_SEED=0
  - SKIP_FINAL_SAVE=0
  - SKIP_IDLE_SAVE=1
  - DEFER_AUX_LOG=1
  - FORCE_NNX_CACHE=1
  - GC_FREEZE=1
  - GC_MANUAL=50
  - MAXTEXT_DATA_RESUMED_STEP=0
  - MAXTEXT_DATA_SKIP_RAW=0
  # Fast resume stays off: the pinned cursor recorder saves the wrong position (ledger #1437).
  - MAXTEXT_DATA_STATE_DIR=
  - MAXTEXT_FAST_RESUME=0
  - MAXTEXT_FORWARD_BF16_ALL_PARAMS=1
  - MAXTEXT_LOG_BATCH_HASH=1

# Four-GPU mechanics test: EP2 Tiny trainer plus one TP2 inference engine.
# Check full decode graph replay across in-place refresh with a small batch.
# Synthetic sibling rewards ensure nonzero gradients despite capped responses.
# Replace YOUR_USERNAME and inspect `plan` before launching.

name = "tp2-refresh-smoke"

[model]
source = "/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/abhishekr/s-c-gpu/s-c-noag-s34521/hf_step63494"

[output]
root = "/weka/oe-training-default/YOUR_USERNAME/open-instruct/runs/tp2-refresh-smoke"
export_hf = false
rollout_sample_rate = 1.0

[launch]
workspace = "ai2/olmo-rl"
budget = "ai2/oe-other"
cluster = "ai2/holmes"
priority = "high"
min_runtime = "0s"
timeout = "1h"
auto_resume = false
gpus_per_replica = 4
memory = "512 GiB"
shared_memory = "64 GiB"

[[launch.weka_mounts]]
weka = "oe-training-default"
mount_path = "/weka/oe-training-default"
===
#!/bin/bash
# Run inside the committed MILES image on two B300s. The checkpoint must fit
# TP1 for the sequential TP1/TP2 greedy comparison (Small does at short context).
set -euo pipefail
: "${1:?Usage: bash scripts/miles/tp2_serving_smoke.sh HF_CHECKPOINT}"
cd /opt/core-rl/sources/olmo-sglang
python -m pytest tests/test_rounding.py tests/test_core_compat.py -q
export OLMO_SGLANG_CORE_COMPAT=rounding
python -m olmo_sglang.validation.tensor_parallel \
    --model "$1" --tp-size 2 --prompt-length 32 --max-new-tokens 16 \
    --context-length 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.8
===
"""Synthetic sibling rewards for refresh mechanics; not a learning objective."""


async def score(args, sample, **kwargs):
    # Consecutive siblings get different rewards even when every response hits
    # the short smoke-test length limit, ensuring optimizer updates change weights.
    return float(sample.index % 2)

content.content:
## Long runs

The four- and eight-node starters are set up so that raising `training.num_rollouts`,
and `launch.timeout` when the run is expected to exceed the starter's timeout (72h
four-node, 120h eight-node), are the only changes a multi-day run needs. Set
`launch.timeout` before the first launch: it is part of the resume fingerprint, so a
resubmission with a different timeout stops with "Run configuration changed". Check each
item below before launch.

### Mounts

`model.source` paths under `/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints` can be symlinks into
`/weka/olmo-3p5-checkpoints` (the H258 SFT export's weights, config and tokenizer
are). The launcher only checks the paths written in the TOML, and it usually runs
where WEKA is not mounted, so it cannot follow these symlinks. A job without the
target bucket fails at model load, not at submission. The starters therefore mount
both buckets. For another checkpoint, run `ls -l` on its files from a job or
session with WEKA mounted and add a `[[launch.weka_mounts]]` entry for every
bucket the links point into.

### Output path and disk space

Write run outputs to `/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/YOUR_USERNAME/miles/...`, not
`oe-training-default` (timing4 failed when that volume filled). One A4B native save
is about 0.81-0.87 TB (model, optimizer and RNG state). With `checkpoint_keep_last
= 2`, `checkpoint_keep_every = 100` and the final save, a 660-update run peaks at
about 2 rolling + 6 milestones + 1 final = 9 saves, ~7.7 TB (the figure in the
starters), plus ~145 GB per evaluation snapshot if enabled (14 snapshots at interval
50, ~2 TB). Rolling saves roll off only after the next save completes, so budget one
extra save of headroom: ~8.5 TB without snapshots.
On November 20, 2026 the volume had 81 TB free of 180 TB (56% used); measure it
again before launch with a CPU job that mounts the bucket and runs
`df -h /weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints`. Do not write to `olmo-3p5-checkpoints`
(95% used on the same date).

### Job timeout and preemption

Run a multi-day job as one Beaker job with a `launch.timeout` longer than the expected
run. `four-node.toml` sets `timeout = "72h"` and `eight-node.toml` sets `timeout = "120h"`. On 8 nodes (eight-node.toml) updates took
~264 s vs ~402 s on 4 nodes (updates 11-30 means at batch 2,048), so a 660-update run
is about 2.3 days on 8 nodes and 3.4 days on 4 nodes with startup (about 35-40
minutes to the end of the first update) and saves. The eight-node run uses 120h, about
2x its expected length; for 660 updates on 4 nodes raise it to about 96h. `ai2/holmes` has no maximum job
duration (`beaker cluster get ai2/holmes`), so the spec timeout is the only limit.

Beaker cancels a job when its `timeout` expires. A canceled job is not preempted:
`autoResume` requeues only preempted jobs, and Beaker's task retries apply only to
failed tasks (the launcher does not set them). A timeout therefore ends the run
without a final save, so leave headroom. Preemptions are handled by
`launch.auto_resume`: Beaker restarts the job and the run loads the newest complete
checkpoint under the same `output.root`; the updates since that save are redone.
Every start appends to `attempts.json`; if you set `launch.max_retries`, allow for
preemptions (default -1, no cap).

If a job does hit its timeout, resubmit the unchanged TOML with the same image:
`MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE=<image id from the launch receipt> python -m open_instruct.miles run <toml>`.
The run resumes from the last periodic save. `beaker experiment resume` applies only
to preempted experiments, so it does not restart a timed-out run.

`core.max_run_seconds` is optional, for clusters or budgets that cap job length. It
counts driver wall clock from driver start; at the first completed collection after
it, the run forces a native save and exits with `workflow.json` status `stopped`
(final HF export and final evaluation skipped), and the resubmission above continues
it with no updates redone. Set it below the job timeout with room for the last
collection (~6-8 min at batch 2,048), the forced save (~10-20 min) and teardown, e.g.
`79200` (22 h) under a 24h cap. Each resubmission pays startup again.

With `miles.wandb_mode = "online"`, all attempts on one `output.root` log to one W&B
run (offline mode, which the starters use, is covered below). On first start the workflow
writes a random id to `OUTPUT/wandb_run_id` (with `OUTPUT/wandb_run_id.json`
recording when it was created and a hash of the model source, data section and W&B
project, entity and group). Every later start, whether a preemption auto-resume or a
resubmission, reads that file and passes the id to `wandb.init(id=..., resume="allow")`.
An explicit `miles.wandb_run_id` takes precedence, and no file is written. If the
stored hash differs from the current configuration, the log shows a
`W&B RUN CONFIG MISMATCH` warning and the stored run is still continued. A new run
needs a new `output.root`.

This continuity needs `miles.wandb_mode = "online"`. The starters log offline, and
W&B offline mode ignores `resume`: each attempt writes its own local run directory
under `OUTPUT/wandb/` with the same id, so syncing them later does not append one
attempt's history to the previous one automatically. For one continuous W&B history,
switch to online mode before the first launch.

MILES logs without an explicit W&B step, so updates redone after a resume (those
since the last save) appear again as extra points for those steps; the later points
are the ones the resumed run trained from.

### Evaluation snapshots

Each starter carries a commented `[evaluation]` block in background mode (interval
50, final). It writes trainer-side HF snapshots to
`OUTPUT/eval-snapshots/update-NNNNNNNN/hf` for offline evaluation, without draining the
rollout engines. To enable it, uncomment the block and delete
`training.skip_eval_before_train`, which selects shared-engine evaluation. Snapshot
export is a synchronous trainer collective, and a failed export fails training. It
requires an image built from main at or after #2293, which brought the writer-only
HF-export memory fix (miles 9eff46a4); with older images the snapshot export can run
out of memory. Snapshot export is not yet qualified on Small. The in-run evaluator
must disable the prefill CUDA graph for Small, because KDA prefill-graph padding
crashes it; the example sets `cuda_graph_backend_prefill = "disabled"` in
`provider_kwargs`. Evaluator job failures do not affect training.

### Changing the start checkpoint

The H196 prompt file records the SHA-256 of the chat template it was rendered with.
If the new checkpoint's template differs, data preparation stops with "Prepared
rendering template hash differs from the checkpoint chat template; re-render
inputs". Re-render the prompts with the new checkpoint's tokenizer before launch.

### Engine drain timeout

The four- and eight-node starters set `core.engine_drain_timeout = 3600`, matching
`core.refresh_request_timeout`, so a final drain or a shared-engine evaluation drain
is not cut off at 900 s (the `two-node-mech.toml` mechanics check keeps 900 s). With
the shipped `export_hf = false` and no evaluation block (or the commented background
evaluation block enabled), no stage that drains generation runs before shutdown, and
terminal refresh cleanup cancels unused generation.

duration (`beaker cluster get ai2/holmes`), so the spec timeout is the only limit.

Beaker cancels a job when its `timeout` expires. A canceled job is not preempted:
`autoResume` requeues only preempted jobs, and Beaker's task retries apply only to
failed tasks (the launcher does not set them). A timeout therefore ends the run
without a final save, so leave headroom. Preemptions are handled by
`launch.auto_resume`: Beaker restarts the job and the run loads the newest complete
checkpoint under the same `output.root`; the updates since that save are redone.
Every start appends to `attempts.json`; if you set `launch.max_retries`, allow for
preemptions (default -1, no cap).

If a job does hit its timeout, resubmit the unchanged TOML with the same image:
`MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE=<image id from the launch receipt> python -m open_instruct.miles run <toml>`.
The run resumes from the last periodic save. `beaker experiment resume` applies only
to preempted experiments, so it does not restart a timed-out run.

`core.max_run_seconds` is optional, for clusters or budgets that cap job length. It
counts driver wall clock from driver start; at the first completed collection after
it, the run forces a native save and exits with `workflow.json` status `stopped`
(final HF export and final evaluation skipped), and the resubmission above continues
it with no updates redone. Set it below the job timeout with room for the last
collection (~6-8 min at batch 2,048), the forced save (~10-20 min) and teardown, e.g.
`79200` (22 h) under a 24h cap. Each resubmission pays startup again.

With `miles.wandb_mode = "online"`, all attempts on one `output.root` log to one W&B
run (offline mode, which the starters use, is covered below). On first start the workflow
writes a random id to `OUTPUT/wandb_run_id` (with `OUTPUT/wandb_run_id.json`
recording when it was created and a hash of the model source, data section and W&B
project, entity and group). Every later start, whether a preemption auto-resume or a
resubmission, reads that file and passes the id to `wandb.init(id=..., resume="allow")`.
An explicit `miles.wandb_run_id` takes precedence, and no file is written. If the
stored hash differs from the current configuration, the log shows a
`W&B RUN CONFIG MISMATCH` warning and the stored run is still continued. A new run
needs a new `output.root`.

This continuity needs `miles.wandb_mode = "online"`. The starters log offline, and
W&B offline mode ignores `resume`: each attempt writes its own local run directory
under `OUTPUT/wandb/` with the same id, so syncing them later does not append one
attempt's history to the previous one automatically. For one continuous W&B history,
switch to online mode before the first launch.

MILES logs without an explicit W&B step, so updates redone after a resume (those
since the last save) appear again as extra points for those steps; the later points
are the ones the resumed run trained from.

### Evaluation snapshots

Each starter carries a commented `[evaluation]` block in background mode (interval
50, final). It writes trainer-side HF snapshots to
`OUTPUT/eval-snapshots/update-NNNNNNNN/hf` for offline evaluation, without draining the
rollout engines. To enable it, uncomment the block and delete
`training.skip_eval_before_train`, which selects shared-engine evaluation. Snapshot
export is a synchronous trainer collective, and a failed export fails training. It
requires an image built from main at or after #2293, which brought the writer-only
HF-export memory fix (miles 9eff46a4); with older images the snapshot export can run
out of memory. Snapshot export is not yet qualified on Small. The in-run evaluator
must disable the prefill CUDA graph for Small, because KDA prefill-graph padding
crashes it; the example sets `cuda_graph_backend_prefill = "disabled"` in
`provider_kwargs`. Evaluator job failures do not affect training.

### Changing the start checkpoint

The H196 prompt file records the SHA-256 of the chat template it was rendered with.
If the new checkpoint's template differs, data preparation stops with "Prepared
rendering template hash differs from the checkpoint chat template; re-render
inputs". Re-render the prompts with the new checkpoint's tokenizer before launch.

### Engine drain timeout

The four- and eight-node starters set `core.engine_drain_timeout = 3600`, matching
`core.refresh_request_timeout`, so a final drain or a shared-engine evaluation drain
is not cut off at 900 s (the `two-node-mech.toml` mechanics check keeps 900 s). With
the shipped `export_hf = false` and no evaluation block (or the commented background
evaluation block enabled), no stage that drains generation runs before shutdown, and
terminal refresh cleanup cancels unused generation.

diff --git a/docs/miles/run-controls.md b/docs/miles/run-controls.md
index 3a5a081d7..f0186fe55 100644
--- a/docs/miles/run-controls.md
+++ b/docs/miles/run-controls.md
@@ -122,7 +122,7 @@ evaluation raises on invalid targets.
 | Dial | open-instruct control and semantics |
 | --- | --- |
 | Save / restart | `save`, `save_interval`, `load`. Saves are synchronous native Core checkpoints with completion manifests and a rollout/policy cursor. `async_save=true` is rejected. Retention uses `core.checkpoint_keep_last` and `core.checkpoint_keep_every`. |
-| Native MoE checkpoint writer | Arithmetic metadata planning, compact storage, and balanced replicated ownership are enabled by default. Opt out with `core.checkpoint_constant_memory_planning=false`, `core.checkpoint_compact_storage=false`, and `core.checkpoint_dedup_save_to_lowest_rank=true`. Each switch is independent. Profiling (`core.checkpoint_profile`) and spawned workers (`core.checkpoint_process_count`) remain opt-in; `core.checkpoint_thread_count` controls thread buckets. The separate dense trainer keeps its own checkpoint path and rejects policy overrides. |
+| Native MoE checkpoint writer | Arithmetic metadata planning, compact storage, and balanced replicated ownership are enabled by default. Opt out with `core.checkpoint_constant_memory_planning=false`, `core.checkpoint_compact_storage=false`, and `core.checkpoint_dedup_save_to_lowest_rank=true`. Each switch is independent. Profiling (`core.checkpoint_profile`) remains opt-in; `core.checkpoint_thread_count` controls thread buckets. Spawned workers (`core.checkpoint_process_count`) do not work in Beaker containers (rebuilding CUDA IPC tensors needs `pidfd_getfd`, which is not permitted, so the first save fails), and Beaker launches reject it; use `core.checkpoint_thread_count`. The separate dense trainer keeps its own checkpoint path and rejects policy overrides. |
 | Final HF export | `output.export_hf=true` in structured files requests explicit driver export at completion; `eval_hf_dir` remains snapshot export for evaluation. `save_hf` remains rejected because native saves do not produce HF output. |
 | Auto resume / launch | Structured `[launch]` controls placement, priority, minimum runtime, mounts and Beaker restart policy. `run` delegates to `build_image_and_launch.sh --miles`; `status` reads a local receipt and queries Beaker. The workflow loads the latest completed Core checkpoint on retry when `auto_resume=true`. The config launcher supports multi-node disaggregated placement and managed judges; raw training files do not submit jobs. |
 | Restart cap | `launch.max_retries` bounds how many times a run may start, default -1 for no cap. Beaker's `autoResume` restarts a preempted task without limit and its own `retry.allowedTaskRetries` applies only to tasks that failed, so neither bounds a run that is preempted repeatedly before it saves. Every start appends to `attempts.json` under `output.root`; once the count exceeds the cap the run refuses to start and says so, rather than consuming the allocation again. The cap counts all restarts, including productive ones, so raise it or choose a new `output.root` to continue. |

Opt out with `core.checkpoint_constant_memory_planning=false`, `core.checkpoint_compact_storage=false`, and `core.checkpoint_dedup_save_to_lowest_rank=true`. Each switch is independent. Profiling (`core.checkpoint_profile`) and spawned workers (`core.checkpoint_process_count`) remain opt-in; `core.checkpoint_thread_count` controls thread buckets. +| Native MoE checkpoint writer | Arithmetic metadata planning, compact storage, and balanced replicated ownership are enabled by default. Opt out with `core.checkpoint_constant_memory_planning=false`, `core.checkpoint_compact_storage=false`, and `core.checkpoint_dedup_save_to_lowest_rank=true`. Each switch is independent. Profiling (`core.checkpoint_profile`) remains opt-in; `core.checkpoint_thread_count` controls thread buckets. Spawned workers (`core.checkpoint_process_count`) do not work in Beaker containers (rebuilding CUDA IPC tensors needs `pidfd_getfd`, which is not permitted, so the first save fails), and Beaker launches reject it; use `core.checkpoint_thread_count`. The separate dense trainer keeps its own checkpoint path and rejects policy overrides. |
 | Final HF export | `output.export_hf=true` in structured files requests explicit driver export at completion; `eval_hf_dir` remains snapshot export for evaluation. `save_hf` remains rejected because native saves do not produce HF output. |
 | Auto resume / launch | Structured `[launch]` controls placement, priority, minimum runtime, mounts and Beaker restart policy. `run` delegates to `build_image_and_launch.sh --miles`; `status` reads a local receipt and queries Beaker. The workflow loads the latest completed Core checkpoint on retry when `auto_resume=true`. The config launcher supports multi-node disaggregated placement and managed judges; raw training files do not submit jobs. |
 | Restart cap | `launch.max_retries` bounds how many times a run may start, default -1 for no cap. Beaker's `autoResume` restarts a preempted task without limit and its own `retry.allowedTaskRetries` applies only to tasks that failed, so neither bounds a run that is preempted repeatedly before it saves. Every start appends to `attempts.json` under `output.root`; once the count exceeds the cap the run refuses to start and says so, rather than consuming the allocation again. The cap counts all restarts, including productive ones, so raise it or choose a new `output.root` to continue. |

## Settings that matter

- `sglang_attention_backend = "trtllm_mha"` for the 5 full-attention layers. On one engine with
  96 forced 4K decodes: 2,881 tok/s vs 2,473 with triton. `fa4` crashes the server: "SM100
  forward with head_dim=256 does not support seqused_q/seqused_k".
- Tuned fused-MoE tiles (`SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR`, see
  [moe_configs](../../configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md)): kernel -9% at batch 96, decode
  +1.6% at R=96. The tiles only take effect in an image built with this branch's
  `configs/miles`; an older image has no file at that path.
- `OLMO_SGLANG_CORE_COMPAT = "rounding"`. The attention trial's HF vs SGLang
  samples have mean |Δlogprob| 0.0155-0.0223 and argmax agreement 98.2-99.4%.
- Admission R=224 on four nodes: `sglang_max_running_requests` 224,
  `sglang_max_mamba_cache_size` 256, `sglang_server_concurrency` 448,
  `sglang_cuda_graph_max_bs_decode` 224, producer budget `async_max_concurrent_samples` =
  224 × engines, `sglang_mem_fraction_static` 0.92, no `sglang_max_total_tokens` key (RunSpec's
  default cap, R × context = 7,798,784 tokens, is above the 3,919,232-token memory-sized pool), and
  `core.refresh_request_timeout = 3600.0` (see [the timeout fix](#request-timeout-at-high-admission)).
  The eight-node example uses the same R=224 serving settings and 3600 s timeout, plus completed-buffer
  factor 1.5, `shared_memory = "400 GiB"` and `RAY_DEFAULT_OBJECT_STORE_MAX_MEMORY_BYTES=360000000000`:
  at factor 4 and Ray's 200 GB default, routing-replay payloads in the full completed queue filled the
  producer node's object store and delivery stalled past `refresh_request_timeout` (run failed at update 7).
- Judge: `timeout = 600` and `chat_template = "qwen3-no-thinking"`. The judge bindings use the
  hashed verifier ids in the H196 `verifiers.json`.
- `two-node-mech` enables the initial serving-weight comparison and repeats the
  standalone/training scoring check every update. These qualification checks add
  overhead relative to the original mechanics run and remain off in timing recipes
  (which retain the default startup scoring check).
- The four/eight-node recipes request 4h/3h of protected runtime, respectively,
  based on historical startup and update times plus headroom. They set a 72h/120h job
  timeout, respectively, so a multi-day run is one job; see [Long runs](#long-runs).

32,768 tokens. A cycle starts at `generation_wait.started_unix` and ends at

final drain and checkpoint/evaluation work are excluded. Each column is its own
median; component medians need not sum to the cycle median. Earlier headline cycle
figures (299/309/399/139 seconds) were not reproduced by this definition.

| timing4n-r160, u40-49 | 4-node, R=160 | 246.8 | 69.5 | 172.3 | 10.3 | 3,414 | 0 retractions, full KV peak 55% |

and actor metric events are in each experiment's `run/checkpoints/` results.
The R96 and R64 runs pass `scripts/miles/analyze_throughput.py` with `warmup=10`,

ranks and all eight R160 ranks completed their requested 30/50 optimizer steps,

### Topology interpretation

- Four-node R96: trainer rollout-wait share is **35.5%** of measured driver-stage

  30.6K useful response tokens/s versus 22.4K for R64, a 37% improvement under the
  strict analyzer. Publication is about 9 seconds/update and is not the largest cost.

content.content:
### Request timeout at high admission

At batch 1,024 (128 × 8), R=224 and R=256 raise engine throughput by 20% and 29% over
R=160, but each request decodes more slowly: about 21.9 tok/s at R=160, 18.7 at R=224
and 17.5 at R=256. A 32,768-token response then needs about 1,750-1,870 s before queueing
and refresh pauses, which exceeds `core.refresh_request_timeout` = 1800 s. Once the policy
produces long responses (from about update 30), whole groups time out and are retried
(883 timed-out group attempts for R=224 over updates 31-40, 622 for R=256 over 31-37;
none at R=160). Updates became slower (medians 351/313 vs 241-247 s), truncated responses
disappeared from training (0.7%/0.0% vs 3.6-3.8%), R=256 filled the KV pool (100%,
51 retractions) and aborted at update 37 of 40 when the rollout failure rate stayed
above 50%.

The fix is `core.refresh_request_timeout = 3600.0` (the per-request deadline in refresh
rollout; nothing else caps it). A timeout discards the whole group of eight, so a few
slow 32K responses waste the other seven samples too. With 3600 s, R=224 (timing4n-r224-t3600,
updates 31-40, 1-indexed; the table's u30-39) ran at 212 s/update mean vs 243 s at R=160 (-13%)
and 401 s mean at R=224 with 1800 s: 0 timeouts, 0 stale drops, truncation 3.55% (r160 3.79%), and generation
wait fell to 33 s, so the run is now train-bound. 4.7% of completed samples took 1,800-2,000 s
end to end. Risk: the longest (>=30K-token) samples finish at policy lag 8-10 (median 9) against
`max_policy_lag` = 12; if responses grow later in a long run, stale drops are the next limit.
This was measured at batch 1,024; at the shipped 2,048 each update takes longer, so a sample
should span fewer versions, but remeasure. The run completed 40/40 updates and then, on that pre-#2280 image (`5c6645da`), exited 1
when the final generation drain hit `engine_drain_timeout` (900 s). On main, terminal refresh
cleanup cancels unused generation instead of draining (above), while evaluation and final HF
export retain generation-drain boundaries. The four- and eight-node examples set
`engine_drain_timeout = 3600.0` to match `refresh_request_timeout` so those drain boundaries
cover long responses when enabled (untested in a run).
One run per arm; no seed repeat. The eight-node R=224 settings come from one 30-update run
(kf-hero-miles-real-8node-b, H258 start).

## What did not work or was not tested

- `fa4` attention: crashes on head_dim 256 (above).
- R=224 at the default 1800 s request timeout and R=256: slower than R=160 and failing on request
  timeouts (above); R=256 also fills the KV pool.
- R=64: slower (396 vs 302 s/update); engines gain throughput up to R=96. In single-engine
  forced decodes, R=144 matched R=96 and R=192 gave +19% total tok/s with each request ~40%
  slower.
- EP4 trainer: untested.

## Code and runtime

The original timing runs needed no Small-specific adapter or weight-sync changes. timing4 ran on image
01M7A0QM57N9499PGFAT73SMF0 (open-instruct a87a0feac). timing4n and r64 ran on image
01M7GA94Q6GKMP2MV2N36YE83Q, built from open-instruct 5c6645da. That is main 28c18166 plus an
SGLang pin with an Olmo 3 sliding-window KV backport, which Small (no sliding-window layers)
does not use. `plan` on main resolves the timing4n config identically to 5c6645da. These
examples have not been run on an image built from main.

workspace/secret names, then inspect `python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/small-mech.toml`
and `python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/small-mech.toml` before using the
[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Build the image from the revision being
qualified; `plan` equality cannot establish runtime equality.

Retain the Beaker experiment link, image ID, submitted TOML and completion artifacts.

## Qualification before a learning run

Copy `two-node-mech.toml` to ignored `runs/`, set a fresh output path and the actual
workspace/secret names, then inspect `python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/small-mech.toml`
and `python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/small-mech.toml` before using the
[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Build the image from the revision being
qualified; `plan` equality cannot establish runtime equality.

Retain the Beaker experiment link, image ID, submitted TOML and completion artifacts.
Verify all four updates, successful code grading, passing initial weight comparison,
standalone/training score agreement, publication acknowledgments and a clean exit.
Inspect `refresh_scores` for mixed-version responses and their historical-prefix and
latest-forward log-ratio diagnostics; see [Core diagnostics](core.md) and
[mixed-policy refresh](async-pipeline.md#mixed-policy-refresh). Those ratios include
policy drift and are not an isolated numerical-parity measurement.

For publication debugging, enable `core.diagnostic_interval = 1` with
`miles.check_weight_update_equal = true` in the run copy to exercise the existing
snapshot/reset/republish checks after optimizer updates. This adds a second transfer
and extra gradient/update diagnostics. The check detects incomplete transfers over
its selected tensors; it does not independently prove the export mapping. Keep a
separate Core-versus-serving score comparison on identical tokens, prefixes and
weights as a qualification requirement. HF-versus-SGLang greedy agreement and the
always-zero `train/ppo_kl` do not establish that comparison.

`train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` (masked mean |trainer − rollout logprob|) is
nonzero on every update, about 0.008-0.010 in the measured runs;
`collection_score_mean_abs` is about 0.0065-0.0067. These combine numerical and
policy differences and do not replace a controlled same-weight parity check. The
metric that reads exactly 0 is `train/ppo_kl`, which is expected with
`use_rollout_logprobs = false` (the old logprobs are recomputed by the trainer on
the same weights) and refresh mode's one optimizer step per collection.

Longer learning runs additionally need native checkpoint/save-resume and evaluation
checks. The historical timing runs disabled saving; the current four-/eight-node starters
enable bounded recovery saves. Their inputs still have no held-out split.

## Open items

- R160 finished 50 updates, then failed its 900-second final generation drain.
  It used server concurrency 320, 192 KDA slots, CUDA graph batch 160, producer
  budget 3,680 and an auto-sized KV pool. Repeat after the terminal-cleanup fix
  and under the intended code-grading and batch/loss configuration.
- Judge latency is not logged per call, so the judge's share of generation wait is unmeasured.

## Checkpoint settings in the current starters

The four- and eight-node templates now enable 10-update native recovery saves,
automatic resume, retention of the latest two saves and 100-update permanent
milestones, plus a final native save. Their 30-update starting budgets therefore
save at 10/20/30; 100-update retention becomes relevant when the run is extended.
The four-update two-node mechanics check still disables checkpoints/resume.
The reported historical timings used checkpoint-disabled runs and do not include
this new save overhead or qualify restore correctness. Measure current batch 2,048
wall time and checkpoint cost, aim for recovery saves roughly every 1–2 hours, and
verify the first save and resume before relying on these settings for long runs.
See [the shared checkpoint policy](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md#recovery-checkpoints-and-preserved-milestones).

## Long runs

input.rationale: 本轮增量（a4cd966a→095d931f）共 19 个提交，分五条线。其一，KDA 权重导出精度（#2339/#2340/#2341）：convert_moe_checkpoint_to_hf 新增 --kda-decay（默认 bf16-grid 的导出值不变但 A_log/dt_bias 改以 float32 dtype 存舍入值；fp32 存每个 KDA 层 A_log/dt_bias/q·k·v_conv1d 五类张量的 float32 master，非 float32 存量双布局拒绝、fp32 需 --skip-validation）、kda_decay_export 包装 save_hf_model 逐张量 cast，并新增 check_kda_export.py 精确核对工具与三份测试——并入已落盘的 u7-l4（update）；export_maxtext_to_hf 的 --kda-decay 三模式与 #2323/#2338 的 Olmo 3.5 Small 8x8x48 overlay、流式加载读前取、JobSet 生产期限共同构成此前从无讲义覆盖的 TPU/MaxText SFT 路线，新增 u7-l6。其二，MILES 服务能力（#2282/#2335）：TP2 引擎 + Core 兼容舍入默认注入 + refresh 引擎面解禁（engine_drain 仍 TP1）+ TP2 专家分片修复 pin + tp2-refresh 冒烟配方与测试，主题独立且量足，新增 u8-l16。其三，长跑容错三件套（#2303/#2299/#2311）：core.max_group_retries 的失败率数学与 resume 宽容、实验性 core.refresh_min_group_size 部分组与奖励基线排除（exclusion.py 声明 honors_exclude_from_reward_baseline）、router TCP_USER_TIMEOUT shim 的构建期注入，合成『多天 run 的服务容错』新讲义 u8-l17；两个新 core 字段与 options.json 新项、TP1/TP2 校验分叉、Small keep_every 50→100 勘误一并牵动已落盘的 u8-l2（update）。其四，运行健壮性与数据链路（#2301/#2314/#2302）：shutdown 有界收尾与 CLI 退出看护、每 output.root 一个 W&B run、跨 workspace resume 与 max_group_retries 运维宽容键并入已落盘的 u8-l3（update）；launch.specification 拒绝 Beaker 上不可用的 checkpoint_process_count 并入 u8-l8（update）；提示重渲染工具链（rerender_prompts、prompt_rendering、run_data 报错指引、source preparation 存 tools）并入已落盘的 u8-l4（update）；Small 配方 launch-ready 默认（eight-node 升 R=224 实测、72h/120h 单任务、长跑检查单、评估快照、W&B 连续性、~0.85 TB/存 的存储预算、缓冲系数 1.5 与对象存储）重写尚未落盘的 u8-l15（仍 new）。其五，回放数据 EOS 掩码（#2328）：numpy_dataset_conversion 新增 replay 掩码函数族并配 mask/check 双脚本与测试，独立成新讲义 u3-l4。identity 内容微调（#2313/#2325）与 AGENTS.md merge queue 注记（#2327）不改变讲义教学结构；上轮已落盘且本轮无涉的讲义全部 keep，上轮未落盘的 u8-l5/l6/l9 维持 update、u8-l12/l13/l14 维持 new 继续有效。

理解校验策略与边界：默认 --device cuda（避免『已转换但未校验』假象）、KDA 1.2B 严格 logit 校验必然失败的已知问题与 --skip-validation + 功能性评估的替代、仅支持本地/WEKA 路径、GDN 混合 MoE 会误入 dense-hybrid 导出器的告诫，以及 --kda-decay fp32 为何必须配 --skip-validation（校验会把参考模型 cast 成单一 dtype，拿舍入值和未舍入值比较）

掌握 --kda-decay 两种模式的语义与适用场景：默认 bf16-grid 适配『forward 见到 bfloat16 舍入权重』的 checkpoint（OLMo-core 训练、MAXTEXT_FORWARD_BF16_ALL_PARAMS=1 的 MaxText SFT），A_log/dt_bias 以 float32 dtype 存舍入值而卷积权重仍 bfloat16，导出值与旧版完全一致；fp32 适配『forward 在 float32 中用这些权重』的 checkpoint（MaxText pre_train.train），把五类张量存为 float32 master；kda_conv_in_compute_dtype: true 的混合 forward 两种模式都无法精确表达，脚本会如实说明取舍

会跟踪 kda_decay_export 的实现：包装 core_convert.save_hf_model 做逐张量 cast（fp32 请求未经过该路径保存时抛错、bf16-grid 两种路径值相同仅记日志），kda_weight_keys 识别每个 KDA 层的 decay（A_log/dt_bias）与 conv（q/k/v_conv1d）权重，cast_for_export 统计 off-grid 元素数

理解 #2293 的边界评估导出顺序：mid_rollout_snapshot 在 rollout 边界返回 None，native checkpoint 到期时已先提交，缺失的边界快照由 driver 经 learner.export_hf 补导，残留的不完整快照以 BACKGROUND EVALUATION GAP 告警

理解 #2301 的有界收尾：driver.close_tracking 经 shutdown.run_bounded 在 120 秒 daemon 线程内收 W&B（超时记入 abandoned 并 dump 全线程栈），CLI（__main__.py）在结果记录后经 shutdown.finish_process 决定退出路径——有被放弃的操作则关闭 driver 持有的 Ray 并以原退出码 os._exit，否则走正常解释器收尾并由 300 秒 exit watchdog 兜底，卡死的 wandb.finish/teardown 或非 daemon 线程不再拖住已记录结果的任务

理解 #2301 的 W&B run 身份：workflow.execute 调 wandb_identity.apply，同一 output.root 的所有尝试（抢占 auto-resume 与重新提交）续用一个 W&B run——首启原子写 OUTPUT/wandb_run_id 与指纹哈希文件（模型源/数据节/W&B project·entity·group），后续 wandb.init(id=..., resume="allow")；显式 miles.wandb_run_id 优先；配置变化仅记 W&B RUN CONFIG MISMATCH 告警

理解 #2314/#2303 的恢复宽容扩展：recovery_configuration_matches 允许 resume 改 launch.workspace 与 evaluation.workspace（迁移整个 study，先认证原 specification；既有任务与工件留在原处），并把 core.max_group_retries 视作与心跳耐心同级的运维参数；startup_timeout 与训练设定仍被拒绝

call_cad2fcc3ad44434180232cb0.head: 095d931f5d2f3ffe02a682d272c012f4feb21767
call_cad2fcc3ad44434180232cb0.rationale: 本轮增量（a4cd966a→095d931f）共 19 个提交，分五条线。其一，KDA 权重导出精度（#2339/#2340/#2341）：convert_moe_checkpoint_to_hf 新增 --kda-decay（默认 bf16-grid 的导出值不变但 A_log/dt_bias 改以 float32 dtype 存舍入值；fp32 存每个 KDA 层 A_log/dt_bias/q·k·v_conv1d 五类张量的 float32 master，非 float32 存量双布局拒绝、fp32 需 --skip-validation）、kda_decay_export 包装 save_hf_model 逐张量 cast，并新增 check_kda_export.py 精确核对工具与三份测试——并入已落盘的 u7-l4（update）；export_maxtext_to_hf 的 --kda-decay 三模式与 #2323/#2338 的 Olmo 3.5 Small 8x8x48 overlay、流式加载读前取、JobSet 生产期限共同构成此前从无讲义覆盖的 TPU/MaxText SFT 路线，新增 u7-l6。其二，MILES 服务能力（#2282/#2335）：TP2 引擎 + Core 兼容舍入默认注入 + refresh 引擎面解禁（engine_drain 仍 TP1）+ TP2 专家分片修复 pin + tp2-refresh 冒烟配方与测试，主题独立且量足，新增 u8-l16。其三，长跑容错三件套（#2303/#2299/#2311）：core.max_group_retries 的失败率数学与 resume 宽容、实验性 core.refresh_min_group_size 部分组与奖励基线排除（exclusion.py 声明 honors_exclude_from_reward_baseline）、router TCP_USER_TIMEOUT shim 的构建期注入，合成『多天 run 的服务容错』新讲义 u8-l17；两个新 core 字段与 options.json 新项、TP1/TP2 校验分叉、Small keep_every 50→100 勘误一并牵动已落盘的 u8-l2（update）。其四，运行健壮性与数据链路（#2301/#2314/#2302）：shutdown 有界收尾与 CLI 退出看护、每 output.root 一个 W&B run、跨 workspace resume 与 max_group_retries 运维宽容键并入已落盘的 u8-l3（update）；launch.specification 拒绝 Beaker 上不可用的 checkpoint_process_count 并入 u8-l8（update）；提示重渲染工具链（rerender_prompts、prompt_rendering、run_data 报错指引、source preparation 存 tools）并入已落盘的 u8-l4（update）；Small 配方 launch-ready 默认（eight-node 升 R=224 实测、72h/120h 单任务、长跑检查单、评估快照、W&B 连续性、~0.85 TB/存 的存储预算、缓冲系数 1.5 与对象存储）重写尚未落盘的 u8-l15（仍 new）。其五，回放数据 EOS 掩码（#2328）：numpy_dataset_conversion 新增 replay 掩码函数族并配 mask/check 双脚本与测试，独立成新讲义 u3-l4。identity 内容微调（#2313/#2325）与 AGENTS.md merge queue 注记（#2327）不改变讲义教学结构；上轮已落盘且本轮无涉的讲义全部 keep，上轮未落盘的 u8-l5/l6/l9 维持 update、u8-l12/l13/l14 维持 new 继续有效。

lectures.practice_task: 对一个小型 SFT 数据集运行 token 统计，画出长度分布；然后用 numpy 转换流程生成缓存目录，对比直接加载与缓存加载的启动耗时；再构造一条 assistant 消息带 tool_calls（arguments 分别为 JSON 字符串与 null）的样本，走 dataset_transformation 的 SFT 行路径（或对照 test_dataset_transformation.py 的新用例），验证模板拿到的 arguments 已是映射、无法解码的字符串未被改写，并解释缓存版本号为何要随之升级。
lectures.title: 数据统计、变换与 numpy 缓存
lectures.topic: 讲解 dataset_statistics.py、dataset_transformation.py 与 numpy_dataset_conversion.py：统计 token 分布、变换数据集，以及用 numpy 预编码缓存加速启动。历史更新（#2300）：Arrow 存不下字段类型跨行变化的 struct，故 SFT 数据集把 tool_calls[].function.arguments 存为 JSON 字符串，而 Olmo 3.5 模板需要映射——dataset_transformation 在分词前解码这些字符串（null→{}，非对象/含孤立代理字符/超递归深度的原样保留），added-token 过滤同步读解码后的文本；旧的 sft_tokenize_v1/preference_tokenize_v1/rlvr_tokenize_* 路径仍按存储原样渲染；DATASET_CACHE_VERSION 升至 v10 强制旧缓存失效。（本轮在该文件新增的回放 EOS 掩码函数族另立 u3-l4 专讲。）

learning_goals: 理解问题背景（ledger H270）：长上下文回放文档以 numpy 目录经 --extra_numpy_dirs 进入 GPU SFT，其 label 掩码全为 True，导致每个文档的最后一个 EOS token 也被当作训练目标，教会模型在超长上下文后停止
掌握判定规则：不以 im_start（id 100264）开头的文档是回放文档（聊天行都以它开头）；只有长度至少为 2、不以 im_start 开头且以 EOS（id 100257）结尾的文档，其 end-1 位置的 label 被清掉——聊天行、以其他 token 结尾的文档、文档内部的 EOS、单 token 文档都不受影响
理解 replay_final_eos_positions 为什么要求 document_bounds 是整文档边界：按 EOS 扫描或按 part 截断都会把内部 EOS 误认成文档末尾

会跟踪 kda_decay_export 的实现：包装 core_convert.save_hf_model 做逐张量 cast（fp32 请求未经过该路径保存时抛错、bf16-grid 两种路径值相同仅记日志），kda_weight_keys 识别每个 KDA 层的 decay（A_log/dt_bias）与 conv（q/k/v_conv1d）权重，cast_for_export 统计 off-grid 元素数

理解 #2293 的边界评估导出顺序：mid_rollout_snapshot 在 rollout 边界返回 None，native checkpoint 到期时已先提交，缺失的边界快照由 driver 经 learner.export_hf 补导，残留的不完整快照以 BACKGROUND EVALUATION GAP 告警

理解 #2301 的有界收尾：driver.close_tracking 经 shutdown.run_bounded 在 120 秒 daemon 线程内收 W&B（超时记入 abandoned 并 dump 全线程栈），CLI（__main__.py）在结果记录后经 shutdown.finish_process 决定退出路径——有被放弃的操作则关闭 driver 持有的 Ray 并以原退出码 os._exit，否则走正常解释器收尾并由 300 秒 exit watchdog 兜底，卡死的 wandb.finish/teardown 或非 daemon 线程不再拖住已记录结果的任务

理解 #2301 的 W&B run 身份：workflow.execute 调 wandb_identity.apply，同一 output.root 的所有尝试（抢占 auto-resume 与重新提交）续用一个 W&B run——首启原子写 OUTPUT/wandb_run_id 与指纹哈希文件（模型源/数据节/W&B project·entity·group），后续 wandb.init(id=..., resume="allow")；显式 miles.wandb_run_id 优先；配置变化仅记 W&B RUN CONFIG MISMATCH 告警

理解 #2314/#2303 的恢复宽容扩展：recovery_configuration_matches 允许 resume 改 launch.workspace 与 evaluation.workspace（迁移整个 study，先认证原 specification；既有任务与工件留在原处），并把 core.max_group_retries 视作与心跳耐心同级的运维参数；startup_timeout 与训练设定仍被拒绝

data.head: 095d931f5d2f3ffe02a682d272c012f4feb21767
data.rationale: 本轮增量（a4cd966a→095d931f）共 19 个提交，分五条线。其一，KDA 权重导出精度（#2339/#2340/#2341）：convert_moe_checkpoint_to_hf 新增 --kda-decay（默认 bf16-grid 的导出值不变但 A_log/dt_bias 改以 float32 dtype 存舍入值；fp32 存每个 KDA 层 A_log/dt_bias/q·k·v_conv1d 五类张量的 float32 master，非 float32 存量双布局拒绝、fp32 需 --skip-validation）、kda_decay_export 包装 save_hf_model 逐张量 cast，并新增 check_kda_export.py 精确核对工具与三份测试——并入已落盘的 u7-l4（update）；export_maxtext_to_hf 的 --kda-decay 三模式与 #2323/#2338 的 Olmo 3.5 Small 8x8x48 overlay、流式加载读前取、JobSet 生产期限共同构成此前从无讲义覆盖的 TPU/MaxText SFT 路线，新增 u7-l6。其二，MILES 服务能力（#2282/#2335）：TP2 引擎 + Core 兼容舍入默认注入 + refresh 引擎面解禁（engine_drain 仍 TP1）+ TP2 专家分片修复 pin + tp2-refresh 冒烟配方与测试，主题独立且量足，新增 u8-l16。其三，长跑容错三件套（#2303/#2299/#2311）：core.max_group_retries 的失败率数学与 resume 宽容、实验性 core.refresh_min_group_size 部分组与奖励基线排除（exclusion.py 声明 honors_exclude_from_reward_baseline）、router TCP_USER_TIMEOUT shim 的构建期注入，合成『多天 run 的服务容错』新讲义 u8-l17；两个新 core 字段与 options.json 新项、TP1/TP2 校验分叉、Small keep_every 50→100 勘误一并牵动已落盘的 u8-l2（update）。其四，运行健壮性与数据链路（#2301/#2314/#2302）：shutdown 有界收尾与 CLI 退出看护、每 output.root 一个 W&B run、跨 workspace resume 与 max_group_retries 运维宽容键并入已落盘的 u8-l3（update）；launch.specification 拒绝 Beaker 上不可用的 checkpoint_process_count 并入 u8-l8（update）；提示重渲染工具链（rerender_prompts、prompt_rendering、run_data 报错指引、source preparation 存 tools）并入已落盘的 u8-l4（update）；Small 配方 launch-ready 默认（eight-node 升 R=224 实测、72h/120h 单任务、长跑检查单、评估快照、W&B 连续性、~0.85 TB/存 的存储预算、缓冲系数 1.5 与对象存储）重写尚未落盘的 u8-l15（仍 new）。其五，回放数据 EOS 掩码（#2328）：numpy_dataset_conversion 新增 replay 掩码函数族并配 mask/check 双脚本与测试，独立成新讲义 u3-l4。identity 内容微调（#2313/#2325）与 AGENTS.md merge queue 注记（#2327）不改变讲义教学结构；上轮已落盘且本轮无涉的讲义全部 keep，上轮未落盘的 u8-l5/l6/l9 维持 update、u8-l12/l13/l14 维持 new 继续有效。

lectures.topic: 讲解 dataset_statistics.py、dataset_transformation.py 与 numpy_dataset_conversion.py：统计 token 分布、变换数据集，以及用 numpy 预编码缓存加速启动。历史更新（#2300）：Arrow 存不下字段类型跨行变化的 struct，故 SFT 数据集把 tool_calls[].function.arguments 存为 JSON 字符串，而 Olmo 3.5 模板需要映射——dataset_transformation 在分词前解码这些字符串（null→{}，非对象/含孤立代理字符/超递归深度的原样保留），added-token 过滤同步读解码后的文本；旧的 sft_tokenize_v1/preference_tokenize_v1/rlvr_tokenize_* 路径仍按存储原样渲染；DATASET_CACHE_VERSION 升至 v10 强制旧缓存失效。（本轮在该文件新增的回放 EOS 掩码函数族另立 u3-l4 专讲。）

learning_goals: 理解问题背景（ledger H270）：长上下文回放文档以 numpy 目录经 --extra_numpy_dirs 进入 GPU SFT，其 label 掩码全为 True，导致每个文档的最后一个 EOS token 也被当作训练目标，教会模型在超长上下文后停止
掌握判定规则：不以 im_start（id 100264）开头的文档是回放文档（聊天行都以它开头）；只有长度至少为 2、不以 im_start 开头且以 EOS（id 100257）结尾的文档，其 end-1 位置的 label 被清掉——聊天行、以其他 token 结尾的文档、文档内部的 EOS、单 token 文档都不受影响
理解 replay_final_eos_positions 为什么要求 document_bounds 是整文档边界：按 EOS 扫描或按 part 截断都会把内部 EOS 误认成文档末尾

会用 mask_replay_final_eos.py 写掩码目录：以构建 manifest（manifest.jsonl 的 part/start/end/length_with_eos）为文档边界来源，新写 label mask 分 part、symlink token 分 part 与 .csv.gz 与 manifest（打包与数据顺序不变），重算 dataset_statistics.json（loss token 数来自新掩码、row-aligned 标记），并拒绝已存在的输出目录

会跟踪 kda_decay_export 的实现：包装 core_convert.save_hf_model 做逐张量 cast（fp32 请求未经过该路径保存时抛错、bf16-grid 两种路径值相同仅记日志），kda_weight_keys 识别每个 KDA 层的 decay（A_log/dt_bias）与 conv（q/k/v_conv1d）权重，cast_for_export 统计 off-grid 元素数

理解 #2293 的边界评估导出顺序：mid_rollout_snapshot 在 rollout 边界返回 None，native checkpoint 到期时已先提交，缺失的边界快照由 driver 经 learner.export_hf 补导，残留的不完整快照以 BACKGROUND EVALUATION GAP 告警

理解 #2301 的有界收尾：driver.close_tracking 经 shutdown.run_bounded 在 120 秒 daemon 线程内收 W&B（超时记入 abandoned 并 dump 全线程栈），CLI（__main__.py）在结果记录后经 shutdown.finish_process 决定退出路径——有被放弃的操作则关闭 driver 持有的 Ray 并以原退出码 os._exit，否则走正常解释器收尾并由 300 秒 exit watchdog 兜底，卡死的 wandb.finish/teardown 或非 daemon 线程不再拖住已记录结果的任务

理解 #2301 的 W&B run 身份：workflow.execute 调 wandb_identity.apply，同一 output.root 的所有尝试（抢占 auto-resume 与重新提交）续用一个 W&B run——首启原子写 OUTPUT/wandb_run_id 与指纹哈希文件（模型源/数据节/W&B project·entity·group），后续 wandb.init(id=..., resume="allow")；显式 miles.wandb_run_id 优先；配置变化仅记 W&B RUN CONFIG MISMATCH 告警

理解 #2314/#2303 的恢复宽容扩展：recovery_configuration_matches 允许 resume 改 launch.workspace 与 evaluation.workspace（迁移整个 study，先认证原 specification；既有任务与工件留在原处），并把 core.max_group_retries 视作与心跳耐心同级的运维参数；startup_timeout 与训练设定仍被拒绝
